_about: Who sends the microsite: identity, contact, booking links, what is worth pursuing, research sources, delivery and the skills or connectors each step uses. Fill every double-bracket placeholder; doctor.py lists any left. Offers live in offers.json and offers.md; locked sprint copy and proof in claims.json; proof stories in proof/.
use_for: [[What you will use it for: selling, jobs, or both]]

provider.business: [[Business name, exactly as written in claims.json about.lead]]
provider.tagline: [[Five to eight words on what you do]]
provider.accent: [[Your brand colour as a hex code, e.g. #2f5d50, or leave empty to use each company's own]]
provider.results_url: [[https://yourbusiness.com/results, or your website if you have no results page]]
provider.photo_alt_event: [[e.g. Your Name speaking at an event]]

about.bio_html: [[Three or four plain sentences about you and the business. You may link the business name with an <a> tag.]]
highlights: [[A result you can prove, with a number]]
about.clients_label: [[e.g. Organisations I've worked with, or leave empty]]

channels: [[How you reach people, e.g. LinkedIn, email, phone, in person, or your own]]
outreach.linkedin_note: [[Do you add a note to LinkedIn connection requests? e.g. no note]]
outreach.video: [[Will you record a short video for each page? e.g. yes, Loom]]
outreach.handwritten_notes: [[Will you post handwritten notes to your best prospects? yes or no]]
outreach.follow_up: [[How you follow up, e.g. one friendly follow-up after a week]]

qualification.goals: [[What makes a deal worth it to you: money, freedom, the kind of work, positioning]]
qualification.icp: [[Your ideal client in two sentences: who they are, size, and the sign they need you]]

criteria.question: How closely do they match the ideal client above?
Is there public evidence of the pain the offer solves?
Do size and budget signals suggest they can pay the fee?
Is the owner or director reachable?
Is there a relevant proof point from our own work?
Can we build a worked example from their public material?

hard_no: No reachable decision-maker after two independent sources
The site blocks automated access and too little is visible elsewhere
ask_before_building: whether to proceed on a weak fit

research.country: [[Two-letter country code, e.g. GB or US]]

sources.question: Size, ownership and structure
sources: The national company register (UK: Companies House; Ireland: CRO; US: the state's Secretary of State filings; Australia: ASIC)

sources.question: What they do and how they make money
sources: LinkedIn company page and staff list

sources.question: Where the work is heavy
sources: Sector public records (planning portals, regulator registers, tender portals, property portals)

sources.question: Real customer pain
sources: Trustpilot and sector review sites (read the 1–3 star reviews for patterns)

sources.question: What they struggle to staff
sources: Current and past job ads (LinkedIn, Indeed, their careers page)

sources.question: Tools they use, and how open they are
sources: Website platform and widgets (booking, CRM, chat, forms)
Each tool's official API, access terms and official or community MCP servers

decision_maker_sources: LinkedIn, viewed by a person or a logged-in browser session (never bulk profile visits)
The national company register's officers list

delivery.publish_subdir: [[Folder inside your website repo that is served at that URL, e.g. public/for]]

integrations.research_data: [[Paid research data connector for enrichment, for example Treg (treg.to), or none]]
integrations.transcription: [[Skill or app that turns call recordings into text, or none]]
integrations.memory: [[Where research and outcomes are filed (CRM, notes app, skill), or none]]
integrations.writing_voice: [[Skill or guide for your writing voice, or none]]
integrations.outreach_method: [[Skill or guide for first-touch messages, or none]]
integrations.email_drafts: [[Skill or connector that creates email drafts, or none]]
integrations.film: [[Skill or app for short films, or none]]

voice: [[Spelling, e.g. British English]]. No em dashes. Plain words.
Never use "not X, not Y" or "X, not Y" constructions, hype-versus-real framing or AI-cliché names.
Use "I" for your personal practice and "we" where the business speaks.
